rows.stem: During electrolysis of water, if the volumes of oxygen and hydrogen evolved at the electrodes are \(\mathrm{V_O}\) and \(\mathrm{V_H}\) respectively, then \(\mathrm{V_O/V_H}\) is
rows.solution:
Electrolysis of water splits it into hydrogen and oxygen:

\(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electricity}} 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

Two molecules of hydrogen are formed for every molecule of oxygen, so the volume of hydrogen collected is double the volume of oxygen: \(\mathrm{V_H} = 2\mathrm{V_O}\), which gives \(\dfrac{\mathrm{V_O}}{\mathrm{V_H}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

This is option (C) \(\frac{1}{2}\).

rows.stem: Which of the following gives the correct increasing order of acidic strength ?

options.label: A
options.text: Sodium chloride < Acetic acid < Hydrochloric acid

options.label: B
options.text: Sodium chloride < Hydrochloric acid < Acetic acid

options.label: C
options.text: Acetic acid < Sodium chloride < Hydrochloric acid

options.label: D
options.text: Hydrochloric acid < Sodium chloride < Acetic acid

rows.solution:
Sodium chloride is a neutral salt (pH 7), so it is the least acidic. Acetic acid is a weak acid: it ionises only partly in water and gives few \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions. Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid: it ionises completely and gives the most \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions.

This is option (A) Sodium chloride < Acetic acid < Hydrochloric acid.

rows.stem: When ethanol reacts with sodium two products are formed. These products are :
rows.solution:
Sodium reacts with ethanol to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas, which is evolved:

\(\mathrm{2Na + 2CH_3CH_2OH \rightarrow 2CH_3CH_2ONa + H_2}\)

No oxygen is formed, and sodium ethanoate comes from ethanoic acid, not ethanol.

This is option (D) Sodium ethoxide and hydrogen.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Sodium, calcium and magnesium are obtained by the electrolysis of their molten oxides.

**Reason (R) :** These metals have more affinity for oxygen than carbon.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Sodium, calcium and magnesium are very high in the reactivity series. They are obtained by the electrolysis of their molten chlorides, not their oxides (for example, sodium from molten sodium chloride), so the Assertion is false.

These metals have more affinity for oxygen than carbon has, so carbon cannot reduce their oxides to the metal. That is why electrolytic reduction is used, so the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
What will happen if :

(a) Xylem tissue in a plant is removed ?

(b) We are injured and start bleeding ?
rows.solution:
(a) Xylem carries water and minerals from the roots to the other parts of the plant. If it is removed, this movement stops: the leaves wilt and the plant ultimately dies.

(b) The blood loses pressure through the leak, which reduces the efficiency of the pumping system. The platelets in the blood plug the leak by helping the blood to clot at the point of injury, so the bleeding stops.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: Consider a circular loop of thick copper wire lying horizontally on a table. Let the current pass through the loop anticlockwise. Draw the magnetic field lines to show the direction and the pattern of the magnetic field inside and outside the loop.
rows.solution:
Diagram: draw the circular loop on the table and a vertical section through its diameter. The wire crosses this section at two points, one on each side of the loop.

1. Around each of these two points the field lines are concentric circles, small and close together near the wire, becoming larger further away.

2. Near the centre of the loop the arcs become so large that the lines are almost straight and parallel, and at the centre they run perpendicular to the plane of the loop.

3. Direction: by the right-hand thumb rule, with the current anticlockwise as seen from above, the field lines inside the loop point upwards (out of the table), and outside the loop they come down (into the table). The lines are closed loops, going up through the inside of the loop and down outside it.

Mark the direction of the current (or the polarity of the cell) and arrows on the field lines; both carry marks.

rows.stem:
(a) What is meant by trophic level ?

(b) On an average, what percentage of energy is transferred to the second trophic level from the first trophic level ? Which categories of consumers do the organisms of the second trophic level belong to ?
rows.solution:
(a) Each step or level of a food chain, at which energy is transferred, forms a trophic level (producers, herbivores, carnivores, and so on).

(b) On an average about 10% of the energy of the first trophic level (the producers) reaches the second trophic level.

The organisms of the second trophic level are herbivores, which are the primary consumers.

rows.stem:
Write down the balanced chemical equations for the following reactions and identify the type of reaction in each case.

(a) Nitrogen gas is treated with hydrogen gas to form ammonia gas.

(b) Lead nitrate is heated strongly to form lead monoxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

(c) A copper wire is dipped in silver nitrate solution and a shining deposit of silver is produced.
rows.solution:
(a) Nitrogen and hydrogen combine to form a single product, so this is a combination reaction:

\(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NH_3(g)}\)

(b) A single compound breaks down on heating into simpler substances, so this is a decomposition reaction (thermal decomposition):

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO(s) + 4NO_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

Check oxygen: 12 atoms on the left, and \(2 + 8 + 2 = 12\) on the right.

(c) Copper is more reactive than silver, so it displaces silver from silver nitrate solution. This is a displacement reaction:

\(\mathrm{Cu(s) + 2AgNO_3(aq) \rightarrow Cu(NO_3)_2(aq) + 2Ag(s)}\)

The silver is deposited as a shining coat on the wire, and the solution turns blue as copper nitrate forms.

rows.stem: Explain the directional movement due to growth in response to touch in a pea plant.
rows.solution:
A pea plant climbs up other plants or fences with the help of tendrils, which are sensitive to touch.

When a tendril comes in contact with a support, the part of the tendril in contact with the support does not grow as rapidly as the part away from the support. The faster growth on the outer side makes the tendril circle around the support and cling to it.

This directional movement is caused by growth, in response to touch, so it is a tropic movement (thigmotropism).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: What is a solenoid ? Draw a diagram to show the pattern of magnetic field around a current carrying solenoid. Name the region of uniform magnetic field.
rows.solution:
A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.

Diagram: draw the solenoid connected to a battery and a key, with the direction of the current marked. Inside the solenoid draw the field lines as straight, parallel lines running from one end to the other. Outside, the lines curve round from one end of the solenoid to the other, like the field of a bar magnet: they leave the end that acts as the north pole (N) and enter the end that acts as the south pole (S), and inside they run from S to N, so each line is a closed loop. Label the solenoid, the field lines, N and S, and put arrows on the lines.

The field is uniform inside the solenoid: there the field lines are parallel straight lines, so the field has the same strength and direction at all points.

rows.stem:
(a) Name the type of mirror that should be used to obtain the following types of images :

(i) A magnified and virtual image of an object

(ii) A diminished and virtual image of an object

(b) Draw labelled ray diagrams to justify your answers in each case mentioned above.

(c) Which of these mirrors can also be used to obtain a magnified and real image of an object ? State the position of the object in this case.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) A concave mirror, with the object placed between its pole and its focus.

(ii) A convex mirror, which always forms a diminished, virtual image.

(b) (i) Concave mirror: place the object AB between the pole P and the focus F, with C beyond F. From the top A draw a ray parallel to the principal axis; after reflection it passes through F. Draw a second ray from A to the pole P; it is reflected at an equal angle on the other side of the axis. The two reflected rays diverge, so produce them backwards (dotted lines) behind the mirror, where they meet at A'. The image A'B' lies behind the mirror and is virtual, erect and enlarged.

(ii) Convex mirror: place the object AB in front of the mirror; F and C lie behind it. From A draw a ray parallel to the principal axis; after reflection it appears to come from F, so produce the reflected ray backwards to F as a dotted line. Draw a second ray from A directed towards C; it is reflected back along its own path. The dotted extensions meet behind the mirror at A', between P and F. The image A'B' is virtual, erect and diminished.

Put arrows on all the rays.

(c) The concave mirror. When the object is placed between the focus F and the centre of curvature C, the image is formed beyond C and is real, inverted and magnified.
